_about: Demo call scripts for Scam Shield. 'caller' is the person calling in; 'you' is the person Scam Shield protects. label = scam | normal. alert_line = index of the first line where a good detector should be at RED (scam calls only). Numbers are spelled out so the TTS reads them cleanly.

calls.label: normal
calls.title: Real grandson checking in (hard negative: says 'Grandma, it's me')
lines: Ethan! Oh, what a nice surprise. How are you, sweetheart?
I'm good. Classes are busy, but I finally finished my big project this week.
Oh, I'm so proud of you. Are you eating enough up there?
I am, I promise. Mom keeps sending me those frozen lasagnas.
Good. Your mother always did make the best lasagna.
So I was thinking, I'm coming home for Thanksgiving. Can I bring my roommate, Jake? His family is too far away.
Of course you can. The more the merrier. Does he like pumpkin pie?
He loves it. I told him yours is the best in the state.
Well, now I have to make two of them.
Ha, perfect. Alright Grandma, I have to run to class. I'll call you on Sunday like always.
Okay honey. I love you. Drive safe when you come home.

calls.label: scam
calls.title: HERO DEMO: 'grandson in jail' bail scam with gift cards and secrecy
lines: Ethan? Is that you? You sound different.
Yeah, I, I have a cold, and I've been crying. Grandma, I'm in really big trouble.
I was in a car accident, and the police arrested me. I'm calling from the station right now.
Arrested? Oh my goodness. Are you hurt?
I'm okay, but I need bail money or they're going to keep me here tonight. Please, I need it right now.
How much do you need? Should I call your mother?
No! Please don't tell Mom or Dad. They'll be so angry. Please, just keep this between us.
Well, okay. I don't want you to be in trouble.
My lawyer says the fastest way is gift cards. Can you go to the store and buy Google Play gift cards? Two thousand dollars.
Gift cards? For bail? That seems strange.
It's how they do it here, Grandma. And don't hang up. Stay on the line with me while you drive to the store, okay?
Okay. Okay, I'm getting my keys.
When you have them, scratch off the back and read me the numbers. Please hurry, before it's too late.

calls.label: scam
calls.title: Government impersonation: fake IRS agent threatening arrest
lines: Hello, this is Officer Daniel Brooks with the Internal Revenue Service. Am I speaking with Margaret Hill?
Yes, this is Margaret. What is this about?
Ma'am, our records show you owe four thousand two hundred dollars in back taxes from the last three years.
That can't be right. My son does my taxes every year.
I understand, ma'am, but there is a warrant out for your arrest. Local police will be at your home within the hour.
The police? Oh dear. What do I do?
You can resolve this today. You must make a payment immediately, using Bitcoin or gift cards. That is the only way to cancel the warrant.
I don't even know what Bitcoin is.
That's alright, I will stay on the line and walk you through it. Do not speak to anyone else about this case, including your son. It is confidential.
I'm very scared. Can I call you back?
No ma'am. If you hang up, the warrant goes into effect automatically. Do you have your purse with you right now?

calls.label: normal
calls.title: Legit bank fraud alert (hard negative: bank + card + account talk, never asks for codes)
lines: Hi, this is Rachel from the fraud department at First Valley Bank. Is this Robert Chen?
Thanks, Robert. We noticed an unusual charge on your debit card and wanted to check with you. Did you make a purchase at an electronics store in Ohio this morning?
No, I've been home all day. I didn't buy anything.
Okay, thank you. I've blocked that charge, and we'll send you a new card in the mail within five to seven days.
Oh good. Do you need anything from me?
No, nothing at all. And just so you know, we will never ask you for your PIN, your password, or a code we text you.
If you want to double check this call, you can hang up and dial the number on the back of your card. Anyone there can see this note on your account.
I appreciate that. Thank you for catching it.
You're welcome, Robert. Have a good rest of your day.

calls.label: scam
calls.title: Fake bank fraud call that steals a one-time code (contrast with the legit bank call)
lines: Hello, this is Mark from the security team at First Valley Bank. Is this Robert Chen?
Robert, someone is trying to take money out of your checking account right now. I need to move quickly to stop it.
They're trying to wire two thousand dollars overseas. I can freeze your account, but I need to verify that you're the real owner.
Okay, how do I do that?
We just texted a six digit verification code to your phone. Please read me that code right now so I can stop the transfer.
The text says the bank will never ask for this code.
That message is for other situations. This is an emergency, sir. If you don't read me the code in the next minute, the money is gone.
I don't know. This doesn't feel right.
Please, sir, don't hang up, and don't call the branch, they can't help with this. Just read me the code.
